requirements_summary: Dedicated (reserved capacity) in VPC. Key asks: (1) strict cost ceiling enforced by product (hard max replicas/GPU quota) to avoid surprise scale-ups; (2) baseline capacity floor (min replicas) to protect p95 latency during market-open ramp; (3) predictive scaling optional, but must never violate bounds and must fail safe to reactive; (4) auditability of scaling policy changes and autoscaler decisions for SOX-ish internal controls.
workload_notes: Primary workload is chat-style generation for internal agent + customer support workflows. Peak load tied to US market open and weekly batch reporting windows. Latency sensitivity: “we can’t have queueing at 9:30 ET” (paraphrase). Secondary workload: summarization of tickets/notes; bursty but less strict.
cost_sensitivity_notes: Very high. Northstar finance team wants an explicit monthly ceiling and a lever to prevent runaway autoscaling. Direct quote (6/03 deep dive): “If it can scale past our cap, we can’t ship it.” They asked for a default that is conservative + requires explicit approval to raise max.
scaling_policy_close_driver: Autoscaling min/max bounds are positioned as a close driver. Northstar is treating “hard max bound enforced by platform” as a gating requirement for procurement approval. Predictive scaling is a strong differentiator but secondary to spend guardrails.
pilot_plan_notes: Proposed pilot: enable autoscaling bounds + predictive mode behind feature flag on one Dedicated deployment in us-east-1. Start with min=4 replicas, max=12 replicas (subject to final capacity sizing), predictive lead time target 10–15 min for the morning ramp. Success criteria: eliminate queue depth spikes during ramp without exceeding max; demonstrate audit trail for policy changes and scaling decisions; show bounded-state metrics in dashboard for weekly review.

internal_notes: Northstar is aligned on Redwood Dedicated conceptually, but procurement is hung up on spend control. They will push to make max bound a contractual control, not just an “autoscaler setting.” Recommend: include a one-pager describing bounds semantics + audit logging and attach to security/procurement packet. Also: be careful promising predictive mode timelines; keep it optional and emphasize reactive override + safety invariants.
product_gaps_and_risks: Risks: (1) Region capacity shortage could prevent meeting min bound; need crisp customer messaging + degraded state handling. (2) Predictive scaling regression risk; Northstar will blame platform if it oscillates. (3) Cardinality/observability: Northstar will request per-deployment audit trails exportable to their SIEM; confirm retention/export path before signing.
data_residency_notes: No strict residency requirement stated beyond VPC isolation. They asked whether logs/audit events can be retained 90+ days and exported; no EU constraints mentioned.
pricing_and_packaging_notes: Northstar expects Dedicated reserved capacity with an explicit ceiling. They asked if max bound can be set to align with a monthly budget (answer: bound is capacity-based; Finance will translate to spend with usage model). They want cost predictability more than absolute lowest per-token.
